sanskrit: karoty āhāram iti māṃ sarvaḥ parijanaḥ sadā yudhiṣṭhirabhayād vetti bhṛśaṃ tapyati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: All my attendants always suppose that I take food, for they fear Yudhiṣṭhira; yet the son of Pāṇḍu knows it well, and grieves exceedingly.

sanskrit: bhūmau śaye japyaparo darbheṣv ajinasaṃvṛtaḥ niyamavyapadeśena gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: I lie upon the ground, given over to silent prayer, on a bed of darbha grass and wrapped in deerskin; and the illustrious Gāndhārī too, under the same vow of discipline.

sanskrit: hataṃ putraśataṃ śūraṃ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinam nānutapyāmi tac cāhaṃ kṣatradharmaṃ hi taṃ viduḥ ity uktvā dharmarājānam abhyabhāṣata kauravaḥ
english: My hundred sons, heroes who never fled from battle, were slain; yet for that I do not mourn, for men know that to be the law of the warrior. Having said this to the King of Righteousness, the Kaurava spoke again.

sanskrit: bhadraṃ te yādavīmātar vākyaṃ cedaṃ nibodha me sukham asmy uṣitaḥ putra tvayā suparipālitaḥ
english: Blessings upon you, son of the Yādava mother; hear now these words of mine. Happily have I dwelt here, my son, well cared for by you.

sanskrit: mahādānāni dattāni śrāddhāni ca punaḥ punaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ me vayaḥ putra puṇyaṃ cīrṇaṃ yathābalam gāndhārī hataputreyaṃ dhairyeṇodīkṣate ca mām
english: Great gifts have been given, and again and again the rites for the dead performed; my years are far advanced, my son, and I have practiced merit as my strength allowed. This Gāndhārī, who has lost her sons, looks upon me with fortitude.

sanskrit: draupadyā hy apakartāras tava caiśvaryahāriṇaḥ samatītā nṛśaṃsās te dharmeṇa nihatā yudhi
english: Those who wronged Draupadī and who robbed you of your sovereignty are no more; those cruel men were lawfully slain in battle.

sanskrit: na teṣu pratikartavyaṃ paśyāmi kurunandana sarve śastrajitāṃl lokān gatās te 'bhimukhaṃ hatāḥ
english: I see nothing further to be requited against them, O joy of the Kurus; all of them, slain while facing the foe, have gone to the worlds won by the sword.

sanskrit: ātmanas tu hitaṃ mukhyaṃ pratikartavyam adya me gāndhāryāś caiva rājendra tad anujñātum arhasi
english: But now the chief thing to be done is what is good for my own self and for Gāndhārī, O lord of kings; this you ought to grant me leave to do.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ satataṃ dharmavatsalaḥ rājā guruḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ tasmād etad bravīmy aham
english: For you are the best of those who uphold righteousness, ever cherishing the law; you are king and elder to all living beings, and therefore I speak this to you.

sanskrit: anujñātas tvayā vīra saṃśrayeyaṃ vanāny aham cīravalkalabhṛd rājan gāndhāryā sahito 'nayā tavāśiṣaḥ prayuñjāno bhaviṣyāmi vanecaraḥ
english: With your leave, O hero, I would resort to the forests, clad in rags and bark, O king, together with this Gāndhārī; uttering blessings upon you, I shall become a dweller in the woods.

sanskrit: ucitaṃ naḥ kule tāta sarveṣāṃ bharatarṣabha putreṣv aiśvaryam ādhāya vayaso 'nte vanaṃ nṛpa
english: It is the custom in our line, my son, O bull of the Bharatas, for all to lay sovereignty upon their sons and at the close of their years to go to the forest, O king.

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ vāyubhakṣo vā nirāhāro 'pi vā vasan patnyā sahānayā vīra cariṣyāmi tapaḥ param
english: There, living on air alone or even wholly without food, O hero, I shall practice supreme austerity together with this my wife.

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi phalabhāk tāta tapasaḥ pārthivo hy asi phalabhājo hi rājānaḥ kalyāṇasyetarasya vā
english: And you too, my son, shall share the fruit of that austerity, for you are the king; for kings partake of the fruit, whether of good or of its opposite.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na māṃ prīṇayate rājyaṃ tvayy evaṃ duḥkhite nṛpa dhiṅ mām astu sudurbuddhiṃ rājyasaktaṃ pramādinam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This kingdom gives me no joy while you are thus afflicted, O king. Shame upon me, dull of mind, heedless, and clinging to the throne!

sanskrit: yo 'haṃ bhavantaṃ duḥkhārtam upavāsakṛśaṃ nṛpa yatāhāraṃ kṣitiśayaṃ nāvindaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: I who, with my brothers, never perceived that you were stricken with grief, O king, wasted with fasting, sparing of food, and sleeping on the bare ground!

sanskrit: aho 'smi vañcito mūḍho bhavatā gūḍhabuddhinā viśvāsayitvā pūrvaṃ māṃ yad idaṃ duḥkham aśnuthāḥ
english: Alas, fool that I am, I have been deceived by you who concealed your mind; having first won my trust, you all the while endured this suffering.

sanskrit: kiṃ me rājyena bhogair vā kiṃ yajñaiḥ kiṃ sukhena vā yasya me tvaṃ mahīpāla duḥkhāny etāny avāptavān
english: What is a kingdom to me, what enjoyments, what sacrifices, what pleasure, when you, O ruler of the earth, have endured such sorrows for my sake?

sanskrit: pīḍitaṃ cāpi jānāmi rājyam ātmānam eva ca anena vacasā tubhyaṃ duḥkhitasya janeśvara
english: By these words of yours, O lord of men, in your affliction, I know my kingdom to be a torment, and my very self as well.

sanskrit: bhavān pitā bhavān mātā bhavān naḥ paramo guruḥ bhavatā viprahīṇā hi kva nu tiṣṭhāmahe vayam
english: You are our father, you our mother, you our highest elder; deprived of you, where indeed shall we stand?

sanskrit: auraso bhavataḥ putro yuyutsur nṛpasattama astu rājā mahārāja yaṃ cānyaṃ manyate bhavān
english: Let Yuyutsu, your own begotten son, O best of kings, be king, O great king, or whomever else you may deem fit.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vanaṃ gamiṣyāmi bhavān rājyaṃ praśāstv idam na mām ayaśasā dagdhaṃ bhūyas tvaṃ dagdhum arhasi
english: I shall go to the forest, and you shall rule this kingdom; already scorched by infamy, I do not deserve to be scorched by you again.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ rājā bhavān rājā bhavatā paravān aham kathaṃ guruṃ tvāṃ dharmajñam anujñātum ihotsahe
english: I am not the king; you are the king. I am subject to you. How then could I presume to grant leave to you, my elder and knower of the law?

sanskrit: na manyur hṛdi naḥ kaś cid duryodhanakṛte 'nagha bhavitavyaṃ tathā tad dhi vayaṃ te caiva mohitāḥ
english: No anger is in our hearts for what Duryodhana did, O sinless one; what was destined to be, came to pass, for both we and they were deluded.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi putrā bhavato yathā duryodhanādayaḥ gāndhārī caiva kuntī ca nirviśeṣe mate mama
english: For we are your sons, even as Duryodhana and the others were; and Gāndhārī and Kuntī are, in my regard, without distinction.

sanskrit: sa māṃ tvaṃ yadi rājendra parityajya gamiṣyasi pṛṣṭhatas tvānuyāsyāmi satyenātmānam ālabhe
english: If you, O lord of kings, forsaking me, shall depart, I will follow at your back; by truth I swear it upon myself.

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi vasusaṃpūrṇā mahī sāgaramekhalā bhavatā viprahīṇasya na me prītikarī bhavet
english: This earth, full of riches and girded by the sea, would bring me no delight were I bereft of you.

sanskrit: bhavadīyam idaṃ sarvaṃ śirasā tvāṃ prasādaye tvadadhīnāḥ sma rājendra vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: All this is yours; with bowed head I entreat you. We are subject to you, O lord of kings; let the fever of your mind depart.

sanskrit: bhavitavyam anuprāptaṃ manye tvāṃ taj janādhipa diṣṭyā śuśrūṣamāṇas tvāṃ mokṣyāmi manaso jvaram
english: I deem that what was destined has overtaken you, O lord of men; by good fortune, in serving you, I shall be freed of the fever of my mind.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tāpasye me manas tāta vartate kurunandana ucitaṃ hi kule 'smākam araṇyagamanaṃ prabho
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My mind, my son, is set upon the ascetic life, O joy of the Kurus; for going to the forest is the custom of our house, O lord.

sanskrit: ciram asmy uṣitaḥ putra ciraṃ śuśrūṣitas tvayā vṛddhaṃ mām abhyanujñātuṃ tvam arhasi janādhipa
english: Long have I dwelt here, my son, and long have you served me; you ought now to grant me, an old man, your leave, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā dharmarājānaṃ vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjalim uvāca vacanaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to the King of Righteousness, who stood trembling with palms joined, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, said these words.

sanskrit: saṃjayaṃ ca mahāmātraṃ kṛpaṃ cāpi mahāratham anunetum ihecchāmi bhavadbhiḥ pṛthivīpatim
english: I wish that Saṃjaya the high counselor, and Kṛpa the great chariot-warrior, together with you, should prevail upon the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: glāyate me mano hīdaṃ mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati vayasā ca prakṛṣṭena vāgvyāyāmena caiva hi
english: For my mind grows faint and my mouth is parched, both from my advanced age and from the exertion of speaking.

sanskrit: ity uktvā sa tu dharmātmā vṛddho rājā kurūdvahaḥ gāndhārīṃ śiśriye dhīmān sahasaiva gatāsuvat
english: Having spoken thus, the righteous old king, the upholder of the Kurus, wise as he was, leaned all at once upon Gāndhārī like one whose life had fled.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathāsīnaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ kurupārthivam ārtiṃ rājā yayau tūrṇaṃ kaunteyaḥ paravīrahā
english: Seeing the Kuru king sitting thus motionless, the king, the son of Kuntī, slayer of hostile heroes, was swiftly seized with anguish.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yasya nāgasahasreṇa daśasaṃkhyena vai balam so 'yaṃ nārīm upāśritya śete rājā gatāsuvat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: He whose strength equaled ten thousand elephants—this king now lies, leaning upon a woman, as though his life had fled!

sanskrit: āyasī pratimā yena bhīmasenasya vai purā cūrṇīkṛtā balavatā sa balārthī śritaḥ striyam
english: He who of old, in his might, ground to powder the iron statue of Bhīmasena—he, seeking support in his weakness, leans upon a woman.

sanskrit: dhig astu mām adharmajñaṃ dhig buddhiṃ dhik ca me śrutam yatkṛte pṛthivīpālaḥ śete 'yam atathocitaḥ
english: Shame upon me who know not the law, shame upon my understanding, and shame upon my learning, for whose sake this guardian of the earth lies in a state so unbefitting him!

sanskrit: aham apy upavatsyāmi yathaivāyaṃ gurur mama yadi rājā na bhuṅkte 'yaṃ gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: I too shall fast, even as this my elder does, if this king will not eat, nor the illustrious Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'sya pāṇinā rājā jalaśītena pāṇḍavaḥ uro mukhaṃ ca śanakaiḥ paryamārjata dharmavit
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, knower of the law, gently stroked his chest and face with a hand cooled by water.

sanskrit: tena ratnauṣadhimatā puṇyena ca sugandhinā pāṇisparśena rājñas tu rājā saṃjñām avāpa ha
english: By that touch of the hand, holy and fragrant, graced with gems and healing herbs, the king regained his senses.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca spṛśa māṃ pāṇinā bhūyaḥ pariṣvaja ca pāṇḍava jīvāmīva hi saṃsparśāt tava rājīvalocana
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Touch me again with your hand and embrace me, son of Pāṇḍu, for from your touch I seem to live again, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: mūrdhānaṃ ca tavāghrātum icchāmi manujādhipa pāṇibhyāṃ ca parispraṣṭuṃ prāṇā hi na jahur mama
english: I wish to smell your head, O lord of men, and to touch you all over with my hands; for my life-breaths have not yet forsaken me.

sanskrit: aṣṭamo hy adya kālo 'yam āhārasya kṛtasya me yenāhaṃ kuruśārdūla na śaknomi viceṣṭitum
english: This is now the eighth period since I took food, O tiger of the Kurus, by reason of which I am unable to stir.

sanskrit: vyāyāmaś cāyam atyarthaṃ kṛtas tvām abhiyācatā tato glānamanās tāta naṣṭasaṃjña ivābhavam
english: And this excessive exertion I made in entreating you; thereby, my son, faint of mind, I became as one bereft of sense.

sanskrit: tavāmṛtasamasparśaṃ hastasparśam imaṃ vibho labdhvā saṃjīvito 'smīti manye kurukulodvaha
english: Having received this touch of your hand, O mighty one, a touch like nectar itself, I feel myself revived, O upholder of the Kuru line.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu kaunteyaḥ pitrā jyeṣṭhena bhārata pasparśa sarvagātreṣu sauhārdāt taṃ śanais tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by his eldest father, O Bhārata, the son of Kuntī, out of affection, gently touched him then upon all his limbs.

sanskrit: upalabhya tataḥ prāṇān dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya mūrdhny ājighrata pāṇḍavam
english: Then King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having regained his breath, clasped the son of Pāṇḍu in both arms and smelled his head.

sanskrit: vidurādayaś ca te sarve rurudur duḥkhitā bhṛśam atiduḥkhāc ca rājānaṃ nocuḥ kiṃ cana pāṇḍavāḥ
english: And Vidura and all the others wept, grievously stricken; and out of their excess of sorrow the sons of Pāṇḍu said nothing at all to the king.

sanskrit: gāndhārī tv eva dharmajñā manasodvahatī bhṛśam duḥkhāny avārayad rājan maivam ity eva cābravīt
english: But Gāndhārī, knower of the law, bearing her grief intensely within her mind, held back her sorrows, O king, and said only, "Not so."

sanskrit: itarās tu striyaḥ sarvāḥ kuntyā saha suduḥkhitāḥ netrair āgatavikledaiḥ parivārya sthitābhavan
english: The other women, all of them, together with Kuntī, in deep sorrow, with eyes brimming over with tears, stood gathered around him.

sanskrit: athābravīt punar vākyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro yudhiṣṭhiram anujānīhi māṃ rājaṃs tāpasye bharatarṣabha
english: Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke again to Yudhiṣṭhira: Grant me leave, O king, for the ascetic life, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: glāyate me manas tāta bhūyo bhūyaḥ prajalpataḥ na mām ataḥ paraṃ putra parikleṣṭum ihārhasi
english: My mind grows faint, my son, as I keep on speaking again and again; you ought not, my son, to distress me further than this.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu kauravendre taṃ tathā bruvati pāṇḍavam sarveṣām avarodhānām ārtanādo mahān abhūt
english: As that lord of the Kauravas spoke thus to the son of Pāṇḍu, a great cry of grief arose from all the women of the inner apartments.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā kṛśaṃ vivarṇaṃ ca rājānam atathocitam upavāsapariśrāntaṃ tvagasthiparivāritam
english: Seeing the king, wasted and pale, in a state so unbefitting him, worn out with fasting, reduced to skin and bone—

sanskrit: dharmaputraḥ sa pitaraṃ pariṣvajya mahābhujaḥ śokajaṃ bāṣpam utsṛjya punar vacanam abravīt
english: the mighty-armed son of Dharma, embracing his father and shedding tears born of grief, spoke these words again.

sanskrit: na kāmaye naraśreṣṭha jīvitaṃ pṛthivīṃ tathā yathā tava priyaṃ rājaṃś cikīrṣāmi paraṃtapa
english: I do not desire life, O best of men, nor the earth, so much as I wish to do what is pleasing to you, O king, scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: yadi tv aham anugrāhyo bhavato dayito 'pi vā kriyatāṃ tāvad āhāras tato vetsyāmahe vayam
english: But if I am worthy of your favor, or am dear to you, then let food be taken; thereafter we shall know our course.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā dharmaputraṃ sa pārthivaḥ anujñātas tvayā putra bhuñjīyām iti kāmaye
english: Then that king of great splendor said to the son of Dharma: With your leave, my son, I would eat; that is my wish.

sanskrit: iti bruvati rājendre dhṛtarāṣṭre yudhiṣṭhiram ṛṣiḥ satyavatīputro vyāso 'bhyetya vaco 'bravīt
english: As the lord of kings, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, was speaking thus to Yudhiṣṭhira, the sage Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, drew near and spoke these words.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho yad āha kurunandanaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahātmā tvāṃ tat kuruṣvāvicārayan
english: Vyāsa said: O mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, what the great-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra, joy of the Kurus, has said to you—do that without hesitation.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi vṛddho nṛpatir hataputro viśeṣataḥ nedaṃ kṛcchraṃ cirataraṃ sahed iti matir mama
english: For this king is old, and has moreover lost his sons; that he should endure this hardship much longer is, in my judgment, beyond him.

sanskrit: gāndhārī ca mahābhāgā prājñā karuṇavedinī putraśokaṃ mahārāja dhairyeṇodvahate bhṛśam
english: And the greatly blessed Gāndhārī, wise and full of compassion, bears her grief for her sons, O great king, with steadfast fortitude.

sanskrit: aham apy etad eva tvāṃ bravīmi kuru me vacaḥ anujñāṃ labhatāṃ rājā mā vṛtheha mariṣyati
english: I too say to you this very thing: do as I bid. Let the king obtain his leave, lest he die here in vain.

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānām anuyātu gatiṃ nṛpaḥ rājarṣīṇāṃ hi sarveṣām ante vanam upāśrayaḥ
english: Let the king follow the path of the royal sages of old; for the final refuge of all royal sages is the forest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā rājā vyāsenādbhutakarmaṇā pratyuvāca mahātejā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Vyāsa of wondrous deeds, the king, the King of Righteousness Yudhiṣṭhira of great splendor, replied.

sanskrit: bhagavān eva no mānyo bhagavān eva no guruḥ bhagavān asya rājyasya kulasya ca parāyaṇam
english: Your reverence is the one we honor, your reverence is our elder; your reverence is the support of this kingdom and of our line.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu putro bhagavān pitā rājā guruś ca me nideśavartī ca pituḥ putro bhavati dharmataḥ
english: I am but a son; your reverence is a father; the king too is my elder; and a son who carries out his father's command is, by the law, truly a son.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu taṃ prāha vyāso dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahātejāḥ punar eva viśāṃ pate
english: Thus addressed, Vyāsa, the best of the upholders of righteousness, of great splendor, spoke again to Yudhiṣṭhira, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata rājāyaṃ vṛddhatāṃ prāptaḥ pramāṇe parame sthitaḥ
english: It is even so, O mighty-armed Bhārata, as you say; but this king has reached old age and stands at the utmost limit of his span.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mayābhyanujñātas tvayā ca pṛthivīpate karotu svam abhiprāyaṃ māsya vighnakaro bhava
english: He, granted leave by me and by you, O lord of the earth, let him fulfill his own intent; do not become an obstacle to him.

sanskrit: eṣa eva paro dharmo rājarṣīṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira samare vā bhaven mṛtyur vane vā vidhipūrvakam
english: This is the highest law of the royal sages, Yudhiṣṭhira: that death should come either in battle or in the forest by the prescribed observances.

sanskrit: pitrā tu tava rājendra pāṇḍunā pṛthivīkṣitā śiṣyabhūtena rājāyaṃ guruvat paryupāsitaḥ
english: By your father Pāṇḍu, O lord of kings, who ruled the earth, this king was attended like a teacher, as though he were a disciple.

sanskrit: kratubhir dakṣiṇāvadbhir annaparvataśobhitaiḥ mahadbhir iṣṭaṃ bhogāś ca bhuktāḥ putrāś ca pālitāḥ
english: He has worshiped with great sacrifices, rich in priestly gifts and graced with mountains of food; he has tasted enjoyments, and reared his sons.

sanskrit: putrasaṃsthaṃ ca vipulaṃ rājyaṃ viproṣite tvayi trayodaśasamā bhuktaṃ dattaṃ ca vividhaṃ vasu
english: For thirteen years, while you were in exile, he enjoyed the vast kingdom held in trust for his sons, and gave away wealth of many kinds.

sanskrit: tvayā cāyaṃ naravyāghra guruśuśrūṣayā nṛpaḥ ārādhitaḥ sabhṛtyena gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: And by you, O tiger among men, with your attendants and through service to your elders, this king has been gratified, and the illustrious Gāndhārī as well.

sanskrit: anujānīhi pitaraṃ samayo 'sya tapovidhau na manyur vidyate cāsya susūkṣmo 'pi yudhiṣṭhira
english: Grant your father leave; the time has come for him to take up the observances of austerity; and there dwells in him not the least anger, Yudhiṣṭhira, however slight.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanam anujñāpya ca pārthivam tathāstv iti ca tenoktaḥ kaunteyena yayau vanam
english: Having spoken these words and obtained leave from the king, and being answered by the son of Kuntī, "So be it," he departed for the forest.

sanskrit: gate bhagavati vyāse rājā pāṇḍusutas tataḥ provāca pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ mandaṃ mandam ivānataḥ
english: When the reverend Vyāsa had gone, the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, then spoke to his aged father, bowing very low, very slowly.

sanskrit: yad āha bhagavān vyāso yac cāpi bhavato matam yad āha ca maheṣvāsaḥ kṛpo vidura eva ca
english: What the reverend Vyāsa has said, and what is your own resolve, and what the great archer Kṛpa has said, and Vidura too—
